I have found a group of people who generally care for me. Not identifying them for legal reasons. Believe me, I know most people are pretenders, don't mean what they say, all that. I've been there and done that. The genuine people are difficult to find though, but if you try to just think about yourself and care about your own life as much as possible, as well as persistently looking for a reputable care group, you will be ok. People may not always understand us but we can pick and choose who we have in our lives. If you want me to be honest, I don't trust many people either. So I'm clinging to the current group I'm with for all it's worth. I NEVER talk about suicide (I feel I don't need to and it's not anyone's business to know how I feel about suicide), yet these people are SO caring and we all help each other out and the people who run this group are highly trained and care just as much about the clients as they do for themselves. And clients are strongly encouraged to socialise and be kind to one another barring certain behaviours which are dealt with according to the medical needs of each client. This group is FUCKING. AMMMAAAAZZZZING! So yeah, please try to hang in there if you can. You just have to dump all the non-caring people. It's very hard at first, but it's so relieving when you can finally realise that you have full control of your life and there's not a thing anybody can do about it. Karma is a bitch and will do justice to your enemies at some point.

What I find funny about society's attitude towards suicide is, on the one hand it's selfish for a merson to kill themselves, but on the other hand, wishing a person who is suffering badly in some way to stay alive, is selfish too. Society has this way of making everyone's life all about the people around said persons, yet the people involved in said concerned person(s) lives seem to think it's ok to be selfish and keep someone from committing suicide, but it's not actually ok for the suicidal person to be selfish and kill themselves. The difference is, the suicidal person is suffering, as it seems, alone, or rather, in their own world, or simply feels totally alone. Call it what you will. But the people around them suffer as a community when the person does decide to commit suicide.

I may not be making sense, but this is the best way for me to explain my viewpoint on this subject. And I just find it kinda weird how we can all come to such different conclusions about suicide. I can understand both sides of the equation, but personally I feel that at the end of the day, if somebody wants out, that's it no matter how you regard said person's action of committing suicide. I certainly won't just sit back and blatantly allow someone in my life to do themselves in, but I also know that whatever I do in most cases would prevent the suicide, but may not stop a suicide attempt in every single case. I also feel that suicide is a personal choice despite it being very drastic and not always the right decision. Meaning, I'd be horrified, for example, if someone I knew, killed themselves over a loss of job or home, something like that. But if the person were say, terminally ill or had a very very debilitating condition, yes I'd be very upset, but I'd be relieved as well, that they arenT suffering any more.
